title: Equivalent of `ifdef` / `#pragma once` in shell `/bin.sh` scripts?
text:
My attempt, atop every one of my—dozens of—shell scripts:
#!/bin/sh

# shellcheck disable=SC2236
if [ ! -z "${BASH_VERSION+x}" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC3028 disable=SC3054
  this_file="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
  # shellcheck disable=SC3040
  set -o pipefail
elif [ ! -z "${ZSH_VERSION+x}" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC2296
  this_file="${(%):-%x}"
  # shellcheck disable=SC3040
  set -o pipefail
else
  this_file="${0}"
fi
set -feu

guard='H_'"$(printf '%s' "${this_file}" | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9_]/_/g')"
if test "${guard}" ; then return ; fi
export "${guard}"=1

DIR=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "${this_file}")" && pwd)
export DIR

SCRIPT_ROOT_DIR="${SCRIPT_ROOT_DIR:-$(d="$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$(dirname -- "$( dirname -- "${DIR}" )" )" )")"; if [ -d "$d" ]; then echo "$d"; else echo './'"$d"; fi)}"
export SCRIPT_ROOT_DIR

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "${SCRIPT_ROOT_DIR}"'/_lib/_common/os_info.sh'

echo 'doing stuff in '"${this_file}"

Unfortunately it always determines the shell scripts as being already-included (so they exit early without executing the script content even-once).
What's the correct way of writing POSIX portable include guards for my shell scripts?

Related:

How best to include other scripts?

How do I source_once in bash?

title: Docker Desktop 1node Kubernetes Jenkins share docker.sock from host into agent docker container
text:
I have been trying to fix this few days, but I have no idea how to make it work.
I have Ubuntu 22.04.5 as a host machine, there is an installed docker desktop running Kubernetes. I created Dockerfile extending official jenkins image as follows:
FROM jenkins/jenkins:2.491-jdk21

USER 0
RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get -y install ca-certificates curl sudo
RUN install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
RUN curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/debian/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
RUN chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
RUN echo \
      "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc] https://download.docker.com/linux/debian \
      bookworm stable" | \
      tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null
RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get -y install docker-ce-cli docker-compose-plugin

ARG DOCKER_GID=999
RUN groupadd -g ${DOCKER_GID} docker
RUN usermod -aG docker jenkins

RUN cd /var/jenkins_home
RUN git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
RUN cd /

COPY daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json

In a nutshell, this Dockerfile aims to add a docker client to the official Jenkins image. It works like a charm, but the crucial part is to connect this docker client with docker daemon running on host machine. The docker group from host machine is mirrored with the GID = 999 and jenkins user is added to the group.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: jenkins-deployment
  namespace: devops
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: jenkins-server
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: jenkins-server
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1000
        runAsUser: 1000
      serviceAccountName: jenkins-admin
      initContainers:
        - name: fix-permissions
          image: busybox
          command: ["sh", "-c", "chown -R 1000:1000 /var/jenkins_home" ]
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
          volumeMounts:
            - name: jenkins-data
              mountPath: /var/jenkins_home
      containers:
        - name: jenkins-container
          image: myregistry/jenkins-jdk21
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
          ports:
            - name: httpport
              containerPort: 8080
            - name: jnlport
              containerPort: 50000
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: "/login"
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 90
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 5
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: "/login"
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 60
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 3
          volumeMounts:
            - name: jenkins-data
              mountPath: /var/jenkins_home
            - name: docker-sock
              mountPath: /var/run/docker.sock
      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: nexus-docker-registry
      volumes:
        - name: jenkins-data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: jenkins-pvc
        - name: docker-sock
          hostPath:
            path: "/host_mnt/var/run/docker.sock"
            type: Socket

Afterall, I am able to make it run, I see the file at /var/run/docker.sock, however when I type command docker info, then I get the following output:
Client: Docker Engine - Community

Server:

errors pretty printing info

I went through all of these forums and everything refers to problem with permissions, however, I am running it with the user (with root privileges and member of docker group) on the host machine and it is linked with Jenkins user UID = 1000 which is member of docker group. Can anyone help me?

title: Azure EventGrid batching delay
text:
When using EventGrid to subscribe to BlobCreated events, then calling an Azure Function to process that batch, how long does EventGrid wait until it delivers the batch?
I want to receieve BlobCreated events after Azure Data Factory is done copying them from a fileserver, but I don't think ADF can guarantee that all the blobs appear in parallel at the same time in blob storage, so the solution I came up with in the end was to call my Azure Function from ADF after the copy activity is done.
I found this comment in the docs which seems to answer my question?

Event Grid doesn't delay events to create a batch if fewer events are available.

I also read here that my function is invoked per element in the batch array? That would obviously defeat the whole purpose of batching...
What are my options to avoid using an HTTP trigger and calling it from ADF?
I considered using a StorageQueue to store EventGrid messages, then trigger my function on a new queue item, and then wait for a minute until the queue is filled up, then start processing the events. This seemed to actually work, but reading 32 messages per request until I got 1000 messages to process felt quite slow...
I couldn't think of a better way to do this, until I decided that for our specific usecase it's enough to have an HTTP triggered function that is called by ADF. The queue solution would be ideal because with the HTTP trigger, I cannot scale out to multiple instances or else there might be race conditions in where a second instance is reading and processing the same blob, but for our usecase this seems to be enough.
Thanks

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS products.products_embedding (

"text" varchar(255),
embedding vector(3072),
metadata json
);

I've installed a vectorscale extension:
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vectorscale CASCADE;


That all worked well and I can see the extension created:
SELECT * 
FROM pg_extension; - that lists my `vectorscale` and `vector` extensions

Now, when I try to query the db, using Java JPA repository, as in:
@Query(nativeQuery = true, value = "SELECT * FROM products.products_embedding ORDER BY embedding <=> cast('[:embedding]' as vectorscale) LIMIT :limit")
List<ProductsEmbedding> findByEmbedding(List<Float> embedding, int limit);

, that blows in my face with the following error:
SQL Error [42704]: ERROR: type "vectorscale" does not exist
I get the same result if I plain query in Postgres:
SELECT *
FROM products.argos_products_embedding
ORDER BY embedding <=> cast ('[0.002165521029382944,..(truncated for brievety)..]' as vectorscale)
LIMIT 10;

Why the extension is not found?
BTW, it works if I try
SELECT *
FROM products.argos_products_embedding
ORDER BY embedding <=> cast ('[0.002165521029382944,..(truncated for brievety)..]' as vector)
LIMIT 10;

I have had the 'vectorextension installed earlier on on the same container, and I believe vectorscale is built on top ofvector`, so that works in Postgres.
It still doesn't work in Java though:
@Query(nativeQuery = true, value = "SELECT * FROM products.products_embedding ORDER BY embedding <=> cast('[:embedding]' as vector) LIMIT :limit")
List<ProductsEmbedding> findByEmbedding(List<Float> embedding, int limit);

Current permissions
I am working with the Azure Video Indexer API in Python to process videos, specifically to index and blur them. While both the indexing and blurring processes run successfully up to a point, I encounter an issue when attempting to retrieve the status of the blurring job after it completes.
When querying the Location URL (provided by the indexing job for checking the blurring job status), I receive valid responses until the blurring process reaches 100% completion. After that, every request returns the following error:
{
    "ErrorType": "USER_NOT_ALLOWED",
    "Message": "User has no permission on account"
}


The access token I am using is generated with the following permissions:

Permission: Contributor
Scope: Account

I suspect this issue is related to IAM (Identity and Access Management), but I have already assigned all meaningful permissions I can think of.
My Goal
My ultimate goal is to download the video after the blurring process is complete. However, I cannot query the API to get the status or the download link due to the above error.
Job URL Format
Here’s the job_url I’m using to check the blurring job status:
https://api.videoindexer.ai/{self.location}/Accounts/{self.account_id}/Videos/{video_id}/redact/?accessToken={self.access_token}&name={name}

Current Code
Below is the Python code I use to query the job status. It works perfectly until the blurring process is 100% complete:
def get_video_blurring_processing_status(self, job_url):
    try:
        # Append the access token to the job URL
        url_with_token = f"{job_url}?accessToken={self.access_token}"
        
        # Send the request to the job status endpoint
        response = requests.get(url_with_token)
        
        if response.status_code == 200:
            data = response.json()
            processing_progress = data.get("progress", "Unknown")
            state = data.get("state", "Unknown")
            return {"processing_progress": processing_progress, "state": state}
        
        else:
            # Temporary hack

            print(f"Failed to get job status. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response: {response.content}")
            return None
    
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Error while checking blurring status: {e}")
        return None

What I’ve Tried

Verified that the access token has Contributor permissions and Account scope.
Confirmed that the token works for other API calls, such as retrieving video indexing status (up until status = 100%).
Attempted regenerating the access token multiple times.

Request for Help

Has anyone encountered this issue when using the Azure Video Indexer API?
Is there an additional permission or configuration needed to access the blurred video status or download link?
Could this be a limitation of the Contributor role, or something else related to how the access token interacts with post-processing operations?

Any insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated...

title: IBM HPU 5.2 - Converting EBCDIC Characters to Blanks
text:
We are using the latest available HPU in our shop, version 5.2.
We need to unload some tables that are quite large (hundreds of millions of records) and transfer those files to an IBM Datastage system for further processing. This system requires the files to be encoded with CCSID 1145. We are downloading DB2 EBCDIC encoded data.
After the data is donloaded and SFTP'd to an IBM ETL datastage process, it is loaded into an UTF-8 Oracle table, then it generates an special file to load an S3 repository using a python program implmenting the BOTO3 library.
We have a problem in a VARCHAR field which contains several characters that cause issues when the file is processed after the Datastage ETL (for example, x'15', x'0d', x'0a', etc.), which encodes the fields into UTF-8. Some characters are encoded as line feeds and carriage returns, causing the processes to fail. Specifically, these characters are not processed correctly when loaded into a VARCHAR field in an Oracle table and then read. Additionally, the file we generate for the Python process fails because these characters are interpreted as line breaks.
We don't have control to validate the input data for the DB2 tables, so we need to "clean" those characters. The simple task was using a column function to change the values to x'40' (BLANKS), and it worked fine. However, as we started to increase the number of characters to change, we finally hit a roadblock and got a -905 error, since the unload was using too much CPU time. We talked with the DBAs to increase temporarily the time for the Batch job but that wasn't an option
So, I started reading the manual for HPU, but honestly, this is one of the hardest manuals I've come across. I think the padding option may help with this, but I'm not sure of the current syntax to use it.
This is the current unload step we have:
//P001 EXEC DBSDHPU1,JOB=XXXXXX,GR=INDBKES,TS=D240129,P=2,S=2
//SYSIN    DD  *                                               
  TEMPLATE DDUNL DSN 'XXX.XXX.XXX.XXX'   
  UNIT 3390DISK                                             
  DISP(NEW,CATLG,DELETE)                                 
  SPACE(5,1) CYL                                         
  UNLOAD TABLESPACE                                       
  DB2 FORCE LOCK NO QUIESCE NO                                                   
  SELECT CHAR('H'),                                           
  A.FIELD1,
  A.FIELD2,
  A.FIELD3,
  B.FIELD4,
  B.FIELD5,
  B.FIELD6,
  B.FIELD7,
  B.FIELD8,
  TRANSLATE(B.CHAR_FIELD,X'40',                               
  X'150D2511000102030405060708090A0B0C0E0F1012131416171819' ||
   '1A1B1C1D1E' ||                                             
   '1F2021222324262728292A2B2C2D2E2F303132333435363738393A' ||
   '3B3C3D3E3F')                                               
  FROM TABLE1 A                                 
  JOIN TABLE2 B
   ON B.KEY_FIELD1 = A.KEY_FIELD1
  AND B.KEY_FIELD2 = A.KEY_FIELD2                               
  AND B.KEY_FIELD3 = A.KEY_FIELD3
  WHERE (A.DATE BETWEEN '01.01.2023' AND '31.12.2023')   
  AND A.COMPANY <> 'STRING 1';
   OPTIONS                                                       
   LENGTH MAX                                                     
   PIC('P',LEAD,'.','00.0')                                       
   REFORMAT (                                                     
    TYPE DECIMAL INTO CHAR,                                       
    TYPE DATE INTO DATE 'DD/MO/YYYY',                             
    TYPE TIME INTO TIME 'HH:MI:SS',                               
    TYPE TIMESTAMP INTO TIMESTAMP 'DD/MO/YYYY HH:MI:SS,NNNNNN000')
   OUTDDN DDUNL                                                   
   FORMAT DSNTIAUL                                               
   EBCDIC CCSID(1145) 

So what we want is to change the translate instruction by a padding or some reformat at columen level, if it is possible, to remove the translate function.
We have a plan b which is to pass the file trhough a IFTHEN sort function, to remove those characters, but given that the file is that huge, we would like to save CPU time.
We tried this at the options block, but it only filled the null values with x'15' at the end of the field replacing only the low-values/null bytes (x'00')
OPTIONS                                                       
LENGTH MAX                                                     
PIC('P',LEAD,'.','00.0')                                       
PADDING(X'15')                                                 
REFORMAT (                                                     
 TYPE DECIMAL INTO CHAR,                                       
 TYPE DATE INTO DATE 'DD/MO/YYYY',                             
 TYPE TIME INTO TIME 'HH:MI:SS',                               
 TYPE TIMESTAMP INTO TIMESTAMP 'DD/MO/YYYY HH:MI:SS,NNNNNN000')
OUTDDN DDUNL                                                   
FORMAT DSNTIAUL                                               
EBCDIC CCSID(1145)  

This is the example of the data in the table:
Key    Column         Data                                                   
       VARCHAR500     9.............99999999999999999999999999999999999999999
                      F1020000000000FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
                      95D512345679AB99999999999999999999999999999999999999999
                                                                             
                      9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999
                      FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
                      9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999
                                                                             
                      9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999
                      FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
                      9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999

And this example the output generated with the latest option block
First part of the file

H012826/12/20245A.99.09999999999.00001.999.v9.............9999999999999999999999
CFFFFFF6FF6FFFFFC1FF1FFFFFFFFFFF1FFFFF1FFF0AF1020000000000FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
8012826112120245159950999999999950000159990595D512345679AB9999999999999999999999
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Last part of the file:

99999999999999999999999999999999999.............................................
FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111

title: Best practice for optional parameter driven SQL queries for use on reports
text:
I am reporting on approximately a million rows of orders for customers.
These orders are for data that needs a lot of calculations, cross referencing and other types of processing. As a result I have written a centralised data retrieval stored procedure that gets the raw order data and performs all the calculations against it (rather than each report including about 1000 lines of T-SQL code to format the data). This keeps the maintenance overhead lower and ensures that data is consistent across a suite of SSRS reports.
In order to provide the correct reporting criteria I have used a parameter block in my stored procedure like this:
WHERE
    (
        (WasteOrderDetail.Active = 1) AND
        (WasteOrderDetail.WasteOrderStatusId IN(2,7,8,9)) AND
        (
            (
                (CAST(WasteOrderDetail.ActionDate AS DATE) >= @LocalStartDate) AND  
                (@LocalStartDate IS NOT NULL) 
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalStartDate IS NULL) 
            )
        ) AND
        (
            (
                (CAST(WasteOrderDetail.ActionDate AS DATE) <= @LocalEndDate) AND
                (@LocalEndDate IS NOT NULL) 
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalEndDate IS NULL) 
            )
        )  AND
        (
            (
                (
                    (ClientHierarchy2.ParentClientId = @LocalClientId) AND
                    (@LocalClientId IS NOT NULL) 
                )
            ) OR
            (
                (
                    (ClientHierarchy1.ParentClientId = @LocalClientId) AND
                    (@LocalClientId IS NOT NULL) 
                )
            ) OR
            (
                (
                    (Site.ClientId = @LocalClientId) AND
                    (@LocalClientId IS NOT NULL) 
                )
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalClientId IS NULL) 
            )
        ) AND
        (
            (
                (WasteOrderHeader.SiteId = @LocalSiteId) AND
                (@LocalSiteId IS NOT NULL) 
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalSiteId IS NULL) 
            )
        ) AND 
        (
            (
                (WasteOrderHeader.WasteOrderHeaderId = @LocalWasteOrderHeaderId) AND
                (@LocalWasteOrderHeaderId IS NOT NULL) 
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalWasteOrderHeaderId IS NULL) 
            )
        ) AND 
        (
            (
                (WasteOrderDetail.WasteOrderDetailId = @LocalWasteOrderDetailId) AND
                (@LocalWasteOrderDetailId IS NOT NULL) 
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalWasteOrderDetailId IS NULL) 
            )
        ) AND 
        (
            (
                (Facility.ContractorId = @LocalContractorId) AND
                (@LocalContractorId IS NOT NULL) 
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalContractorId IS NULL) 
            )
        ) AND 
        (
            (
                (WasteOrderDetail.FacilityId = @LocalFacilityId) AND
                (@LocalFacilityId IS NOT NULL) 
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalFacilityId IS NULL) 
            )
        ) AND 
        (
            (
                (DATEPART(YEAR,WasteOrderDetail.ActionDate) = @LocalYear) AND
                (@LocalYear IS NOT NULL)
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalYear IS NULL)
            )
        ) AND 
        (
            (
                (DATEPART(MONTH,WasteOrderDetail.ActionDate) = @LocalMonth) AND
                (@LocalMonth IS NOT NULL) 
            ) OR
            (
                (@LocalMonth IS NULL)
            )
        ) AND
        (
            (@LocalClientId IS NOT NULL) OR
            (@LocalSiteId IS NOT NULL) OR
            (@LocalWasteOrderHeaderId IS NOT NULL) OR
            (@LocalWasteOrderDetailId IS NOT NULL)  OR
            (@LocalContractorId IS NOT NULL) OR
            (@LocalFacilityId IS NOT NULL) OR
            (@LocalStartDate IS NOT NULL) OR
            (@LocalEndDate IS NOT NULL) OR
            (@LocalYear IS NOT NULL) OR
            (@LocalMonth IS NOT NULL) 
        )
    )

I move the stored procedure input parameters into local parameters to avoid parameter sniffing issues.
This solution is far from ideal as it can cause some issues with the execution plan (I did want to use a view for the centralised retrieval using a CTE but the conditional parameters ruined the performance). I have read that blocks of conditional parameters can be bad but I can see no alternative.
What is the generally accepted solution for providing maintainable and centralised data retrieval when the data requires parameters for selection?

title: IFC Visibility Issue: APS Viewer vs ACC Viewer Behavior with Viewer.ShowAll()
text:
We are currently working with the APS Viewer and have encountered an issue related to element visibility when working with IFC files.
Usually, IFC element such as IFC Spaces and IFC Openings, are hidden by default in most viewers. When resetting the model's visibility, the expected behavior is for these originally hidden elements to remain hidden.
However, in the APS Viewer, when we reset visibility using
viewer.showAll(),

these originally hidden elements become visible again. Interestingly, we observed the same behavior on the default APS Viewer (viewer.autodesk.com).
In contrast, the ACC Viewer behaves as expected—when using the "Show All Objects" option via the right-click menu, originally hidden elements remain hidden.
Upon investigation, we noticed that both ACC Viewer and APS Viewer use the same
viewer.showAll() 

API. This suggests that the ACC Viewer must have an additional mechanism or implementation to handle originally hidden elements effectively.
ACC Viewer
viewer.autodesk
We would greatly appreciate any insights or details regarding the implementation differences or specific APIs used in the ACC Viewer to achieve this behavior.
Looking forward to your guidance.

title: Handle an option only if another option is used
text:
I need to process command-line options from my Python script that correspond to the syntax
tesy.py [-h] [-a [-b]]

(This is just a simplistic example illustrating the problem; in reality my script has lots of other options.)
That is, the following synaxes are correct
test.py
test.py -h
test.py -a
test.py -a -b

but the following one is not
test.py -b

because the option -a is not specified.
Can this been done with argparse in an elegant way?
The obvious way doesn't work:
from argparse import ArgumentParser

parser = ArgumentParser(description='Test script')
parser.add_argument('-a', action='store_true')
parser.add_argument('-b', action='store_true')
args = parser.parse_args()

because it would accept the invalid syntax test.py -b. Now, I could check manually if the option -a is present when the option -b is given and issue an error otherwise:
from argparse import ArgumentParser

parser = ArgumentParser(description='Test script')
parser.add_argument('-a', action='store_true')
parser.add_argument('-b', action='store_true')
args = parser.parse_args()
if args.b and not args.a:
    parser.error('Option -b requires option -a.')

but that's somewhat inellegant. Is there a way for argparse to handle the syntax itself?
Or I could use some trickery (thanks, ChatGPT) like this:
from argparse import ArgumentParser

parser = ArgumentParser(description='Test script')
parser.add_argument('-a', action='store_true')
args, unknown = parser.parse_known_args()
if args.a:
    parser.add_argument('-b', action='store_true')
    args = parser.parse_args()
else:
    args = parser.parse_args(unknown)

and this works - but the help text (test.py -h) does not mention the option -b at all. In theory, I could override the help text by using the usage= argument of ArgumentParser but this is error-prone - my script is much more complex than this simplistic example, has lots of options, is still under development, and if I have to maintain my own usage text, I might forget to update it when I add, remove, or modify an option.
I can't use a sub-parser because those work only with positional arguments - not with options.
Maybe what I want can be done with docopt but my script's command-line processing is already built around argparse and I'd rather not have to rewrite that.
So, is there an elegant way of doing what I want with argparse? Or should I just swallow my pride and use one of the klunky ones?

title: How to Obfuscate Code in a Closed-Source SDK While Keeping Compose Function Parameters Intact?
text:
I am developing a closed-source Android SDK where I need to obfuscate the implementation code to protect it from being reverse-engineered. However, I also need to expose certain functions to developers integrating this SDK.
One of the functions I want to expose is a Jetpack Compose function. When I enable obfuscation (minifyEnabled = true), the Compose function:
Loses its parameter names — This makes it difficult for developers to understand the function signature.
Generates additional parameters (e.g., Composer var4, int var5, int var6) which are not present in the original function definition — leading to ambiguity and confusion for developers using the SDK.
Example Code:
Expected Function Signature:
@Composable
fun BannerCarouselWithWebView(
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    showWidgetTitle: Boolean = true,
    showWebViewBackButton: Boolean = true,
    configMap: Map<String, String>,
)

Actual Output After Obfuscation:
BannerCarouselWithWebView(
    Modifier var0, boolean var1, boolean var2, Map<String, String> var3, Composer var4, int var5, int var6
)

What I Need:

Keep the parameter names intact for the Compose function.
Avoid adding extra parameters like Composer and int values during
obfuscation.
Obfuscate the rest of the SDK code while preserving this specific
Compose function as-is.

What I’ve Tried:

Added ProGuard rules to exclude the Compose function, but this led to
incomplete obfuscation or runtime errors.
Used @Keep annotation on the Compose function, which prevented
obfuscation entirely but didn’t resolve the parameter transformation
issue.
Experimented with R8 rules to customize behavior, but
Compose-specific changes still persisted.

Question:

How can I configure ProGuard or R8 rules to preserve the Compose
function signature without transforming parameters while obfuscating
the rest of the SDK?
Is there a Compose-specific rule or compiler   option that prevents
these extra parameters from being added?
Are there any best practices for exposing Compose functions in
closed-source SDKs while maintaining clear API definitions?

Any insights or solutions would be greatly appreciated!

title: Best Practice for Creating a Model's Record in `post_save` Signal While Maintaining Data Integrity in Django
text:
I am working on a Django application where I need to automatically create a Setting record with default values whenever a new User is created. My current implementation uses the post_save signal of the User model to handle this logic.
from django.db.models.signals import post_save
from django.db import transaction
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from myapp.models import Setting

@receiver(post_save, sender=User)
def create_default_setting(sender, instance, created, **kwargs):
    if created:
        transaction.on_commit(lambda: Setting.objects.create(user=instance))

I used transaction.on_commit to make sure that the creation of the Setting record happens only after the User creation transaction is committed, to avoid issues where the User instance might not yet exist in the database. However, this separates the Setting creation from the User creation transaction. If for any reason the Setting creation fails (e.g., validation errors, database issues), I end up with a User record without a corresponding Setting, which violates data integrity.
On the other hand, if I don't use transaction.on_commit and create the Setting directly in the post_save signal, there is a risk of attempting to create a Setting record before the User instance is fully saved in the database, or creating a Setting even when the User creation fails due to an uncommitted or rolled-back transaction.
This leaves me with two imperfect solutions:

Using transaction.on_commit: Ensures the User is committed before the Setting creation but risks incomplete data in case the Setting creation fails.
Without transaction.on_commit: Risks trying to create a Setting before the User is fully saved or creating unnecessary Setting records in failed transactions.

My Questions:

What is the best practice for handling such scenarios in Django where one model's record depends on the successful creation of another model's record?

Is there a way to ensure that the User and Setting records are created within the same transaction to guarantee data integrity while avoiding race conditions or premature queries?


Any guidance or suggestions would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!

title: Django Channels: Maintaining WebSocket Authentication Across Multiple Consumers
text:
I am developing a dashboard using Django Channels and have implemented two WebSocket consumers—UserConsumer and RequestConsumer—to handle user authentication and requests, respectively.
Problem
After successfully logging in through UserConsumer, the session is not shared with RequestConsumer. As a result, the second WebSocket connection (RequestConsumer) detects the user as unauthenticated and immediately closes the connection.
Implementation Details
Authentication in UserConsumer:
Users authenticate via an OTP code sent to their mobile number.
The login method saves the session using self.scope["session"].save().
class UserConsumer(AsyncJsonWebsocketConsumer):
    async def connect(self):
        await self.accept()

    async def user_login(self, content):
        verify_code = self.scope.get("verify_code")
        code = content.get("code")
        mobile = self.scope.get("mobile")
        if mobile and verify_code and code == verify_code:
            user = await load_user_by_mobile(mobile)
            del self.scope["verify_code"]
            await login(self.scope, user)
            await database_sync_to_async(self.scope["session"].save)()
            await self.send_json({"code": 200})
        else:
            await self.send_json({"code": 400})

Session Validation in RequestConsumer:
class RequestConsumer(AsyncWebsocketConsumer):
    async def connect(self):
        self.user = self.scope['user']
        if self.user.is_authenticated:
            await self.accept()
        else:
            await self.close()

ASGI Application Configuration:
application = ProtocolTypeRouter({
    "http": django_asgi_app,
    "websocket": AllowedHostsOriginValidator(
        AuthMiddlewareStack(
            URLRouter([
                path("user/", UserConsumer.as_asgi()),
                path("requests/", RequestConsumer.as_asgi()),
            ])
        )
    ),
})

Session Settings:
SESSION_ENGINE = 'django.contrib.sessions.backends.db'
SESSION_COOKIE_NAME = 'sessionid'
SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True
SESSION_EXPIRE_AT_BROWSER_CLOSE = False
SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST = True

Client Test Script:
const socket1 = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8000/user/");

socket1.onmessage = (event) => {
  const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
  if (data.code === 200) {
    const socket2 = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8000/requests/");
  }
};

Observations

The user_login method works, and the user is authenticated within
UserConsumer.
However, when the second WebSocket (RequestConsumer) connects, the
user is no longer recognized as authenticated, and the socket closes.
No session cookies appear in the browser, raising concerns about
session persistence across consumers.

Key Questions

How can I persist authentication across multiple WebSocket
connections using Django Channels?

Should cookies or headers be explicitly sent to the browser for
session management in WebSockets?

Is there an issue with the middleware configuration or session
handling in this implementation?


Any help in resolving this would be greatly appreciated!

title: How to do a clean install of python from source in a Docker container? (Image gets very large)
text:
Currently I have to create Docker images that build python from source (for example we do need two different python versions in a container, one python version for building and one for testing the application, also we need to exactly specify the python version we want to install and newer versions are not supported via apt install for example).
My Problem is a.t.m. that the size of the image gets really large if you build python from source and yet I do not fully understand why.
Let's take the following image as an example:
# we start with prebuild python image to set system python to 3.13
FROM WWW.SOMEURL.COM/python:3.13-slim-bullseye  

# now we install the build dependencies required to build python from source
RUN apt update -y &&\
    apt upgrade -y &&\
    apt-get install --no-install-recommends --yes \
        build-essential \
        zlib1g-dev \
        libncurses5-dev \
        libgdbm-dev \
        libnss3-dev \
        libssl-dev \
        libreadline-dev \
        libffi-dev \
        libsqlite3-dev \
        libbz2-dev \
        git \
        wget &&\
    apt-get clean

# next we altinstall another python version by building it from source
RUN   cd /usr/src &&\
      wget "https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.11.11/Python-3.11.11.tgz" &&\
      tar xzf "Python-3.11.11.tgz" &&\
      cd "Python-3.11.11" &&\
      ./configure &&\
      make altinstall

# finally we remove the build dependencies to safe some space
RUN apt-get remove --purge  -y \
        build-essential \
        zlib1g-dev \
        libncurses5-dev \
        libgdbm-dev \
        libnss3-dev \
        libssl-dev \
        libreadline-dev \
        libffi-dev \
        libsqlite3-dev \
        libbz2-dev \
        git \
        wget &&\
    apt-get autoremove --purge -y &&\
    apt-get autoclean -y

# verify installation
RUN echo "DEBUG: Path to alt python: $(which python3.11) which has version $(python3.11 --version)"

For me this process results in a very large image, while the python installation itself should not be that large (~150-200 MB on a local machine). However, it seems like the pure installation of python from source adds around 800MB to the image. Why is this the case?
Thank you for your help!

New Dockerfile according to answers, that greatly reduces (~50%) the final size of the image:
# we start with prebuild python image to set system python to 3.13, if you dont need that you can just use any other image and perform the same steps (maybe swap altinstall to install)
FROM WWW.SOMEURL.COM/python:3.13-slim-bullseye  

# install and remove build dependencies in a single stage
RUN bash install_build_deps.sh && \
    bash altinstall_python.sh && \
    bash remove_build_deps.sh

# verify installation
RUN echo "DEBUG: Path to alt python: $(which python3.11) which has version $(python3.11 --version)"

Script install_build_deps.sh (addition of removing /var/lib/apt/lists/*):
apt-get update -y
apt-get upgrade -y
apt-get install --no-install-recommends --yes
   build-essential
   zlib1g-dev
   libncurses5-dev
   libgdbm-dev
   libnss3-dev
   libssl-dev
   libreadline-dev
   libffi-dev
   libsqlite3-dev
   libbz2-dev
   wget
rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
apt-get clean

Script altinstall_python.sh (delete tarball and added files to /usr/local/src):
cd "/usr/local/src"
wget "https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.11.11/Python-3.11.11.tgz"
tar xzf "Python-3.11.11.tgz"
cd "Python-3.11.11"
./configure
make altinstall
rm "Python-3.11.11.tgz"
rm -r Python-3.11.11

Script remove_build_deps.sh:
apt-get remove --purge  -y \
   build-essential \
   zlib1g-dev \
   libncurses5-dev \
   libgdbm-dev \
   libnss3-dev \
   libssl-dev \
   libreadline-dev \
   libffi-dev \
   libsqlite3-dev \
   libbz2-dev \
   wget &&\
apt-get autoremove --purge -y &&\
apt-get autoclean -y

Thanks a lot for the help, if there are further optimizations, let me know and I will update this, if somebody wants to use it as a reference.

df = pd.DataFrame([{'id': i, 'min_latency': pd.NaT} for i in range(10)])

df = pd.DataFrame([{'id': i, 'min_latency': pd.NaT} for i in range(10)] + [{'id': -1, 'min_latency': dt.timedelta(seconds=3)}])

title: Improve computational time and memory usage of the calculation of a large Matrix that has four loops
text:
I want to calculate a Matrix G that its elements is a scalar and are calculated as:

I want to calculated this matrix for a large n > 10000, d>30. My code is below but it has a huge overhead and it still takes very long time.
How can I make this computation at the fastest possible way? Without using GPU and Minimize the memory usage.
import numpy as np
from sklearn.gaussian_process.kernels import Matern
from tqdm import tqdm
from joblib import Parallel, delayed

# Pre-flattened computation to minimize data transfer overhead
def precompute_differences(R, Z):
    n, d        = R.shape
    R_diff_flat = (R[:, None, :] - R[None, :, :]).reshape(n * n, d)
    Z_diff      = Z[:, None, :] - Z[None, :, :]
    return R_diff_flat, Z_diff

def compute_G_row(i, R_diff_flat, Z_diff, W, gamma_val, kernel, n, d):
    """
    Compute the i-th row for j >= i and store them in a temporary array.
    """
    row_values = np.zeros(n)
    for j in range(i, n):
        Z_ij   = gamma_val * Z_diff[i, j].reshape(1, d)
        K_flat = kernel(R_diff_flat, Z_ij)
        K_ij   = K_flat.reshape(n, n)
        row_values[j] = np.sum(W * K_ij)
    return i, row_values

def compute_G(M, gamma, R, Z, nu=1.5, length_scale=1.0, use_parallel=True):
    """
    Compute the G matrix with fewer kernel evaluations by exploiting symmetry:
    G[i,j] = G[j,i]. We only compute for j >= i, then mirror the result.
    """
    R = np.asarray(R)
    Z = np.asarray(Z)
    M = np.asarray(M).reshape(-1, 1)  # ensure (n,1)
    n, d = R.shape

    # Precompute data
    R_diff_flat, Z_diff = precompute_differences(R, Z)
    W = M @ M.T  # Weight matrix

    G = np.zeros((n, n))

    kernel = Matern(length_scale=length_scale, nu=nu)

    if use_parallel and n > 1:
        # Parallel computation
        results = Parallel(n_jobs=-1)(
            delayed(compute_G_row)(i, R_diff_flat, Z_diff, W, gamma, kernel, n, d)
            for i in tqdm(range(n), desc="Computing G matrix")
        )
    else:
        # Single-threaded computation
        results = []
        for i in tqdm(range(n), desc="Computing G matrix"):
            row_values = np.zeros(n)
            for j in range(i, n):
                Z_ij   = gamma * Z_diff[i, j].reshape(1, d)
                K_flat = kernel(R_diff_flat, Z_ij)
                K_ij   = K_flat.reshape(n, n)
                row_values[j] = np.sum(W * K_ij)
            results.append((i, row_values))

    # Sort and fill final G by symmetry
    results.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    for i, row_vals in results:
        for j in range(i, n):
            G[i, j] = row_vals[j]
            G[j, i] = row_vals[j]  # mirror for symmetry

    # Delete auxiliary variables to save memory
    del R_diff_flat, Z_diff, W, kernel, results

    # Optional checks
    is_symmetric = np.allclose(G, G.T, atol=1e-8)
    eigenvalues = np.linalg.eigvalsh(G)
    is_semi_positive_definite = np.all(eigenvalues >= -1e-8)
    print(f"G is semi-positive definite: {is_semi_positive_definite}")
    print(f"G is symmetric: {is_symmetric}")

    # Delete all local auxiliary variables except G to save memory
    local_vars = list(locals().keys())
    for var_name in local_vars:
        if var_name not in ["G"]:
            del locals()[var_name]

    return G

Toy Example
# Example usage:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    __spec__ = None
    n = 20
    d = 10
    gamma = 0.9
    R = np.random.rand(n, d)
    Z = np.random.rand(n, d)
    M = np.random.rand(n, 1)

    G = compute_G(M, gamma, R, Z, nu=1.5, length_scale=1.0, use_parallel=True)
    print("G computed with shape:", G.shape)

title: Sleeping Ubuntu with a bash script based on docker network traffic
text:
Context

I have a personal homeserver running Ubuntu. I would like it to sleep after the server activity has slowed down to help reduce its power consumption.
I wrote a shell script to check docker bridge network usage. If its below a certain MB threshold I deem the server inactive and suspend it.
I have this script run every 2 hours with cron (for now I'm making it run every 2 minutes for debugging)
I'm running into issues getting this to work properly.

What I've done

First I ssh into my home server
Then I wrote the code for the bash script:

#!/bin/bash

# Usage threshold in bytes (2MB = 5 * 1024 * 1024)
THRESHOLD=$((2 * 1024 * 1024))
INTERVAL=5

calculate_docker_traffic() {
    RX_BEFORE=0
    TX_BEFORE=0

    for IFACE in $(ls /sys/class/net | grep '^br-'); do
        RX_BEFORE=$((RX_BEFORE + $(cat /sys/class/net/$IFACE/statistics/rx_bytes)))
        TX_BEFORE=$((TX_BEFORE + $(cat /sys/class/net/$IFACE/statistics/tx_bytes)))
    done

    echo "$RX_BEFORE $TX_BEFORE"
}

read RX_BEFORE TX_BEFORE < <(calculate_docker_traffic)
sleep $INTERVAL
read RX_AFTER TX_AFTER < <(calculate_docker_traffic)
RX_DIFF=$((RX_AFTER - RX_BEFORE))
TX_DIFF=$((TX_AFTER - TX_BEFORE))
TOTAL_USAGE=$((RX_DIFF + TX_DIFF))

echo $TOTAL_USAGE
if (( TOTAL_USAGE < THRESHOLD )); then
    echo "Docker network usage is below threshold. Suspending system."
    sudo /usr/bin/systemctl suspend
else
    echo "Docker network usage is above threshold. Staying awake."
fi


Then I added it as a cronjob with sudo crontab -e. For debugging I made it run every 2 minutes. I also adding the logger part at the end so I could see the logs of it:

*/2 * * * * /bin/bash /home/drew/auto_sleep.sh | logger -t mycmd


I can grep the logs and see that its running okay with

grep 'mycmd' /var/log/syslog

With the output:
2024-12-30T20:28:01.466156+00:00 yepyolab CRON[2584227]: (root) CMD (/bin/bash /home/drew/auto_sleep.sh | logger -t mycmd)
2024-12-30T20:28:06.479349+00:00 yepyolab mycmd: 7927
2024-12-30T20:28:06.479463+00:00 yepyolab mycmd: Docker network usage is below threshold. Suspending system.


But the issue is the server never suspends

Things I've tried:

added my script to sudo crontab -e instead of crontab -e
updated suspend to not require a password by doing sudo visudo and then drew ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl suspend
used the full path of /usr/bin/systemctl suspend
added a --force to /usr/bin/systemctl suspend --force
Tried manually hard coding the password with $echo <password> | sudo -S systemctl suspend
Tried using sudo pm-suspend

Questions:

Is it not suspending because I'm doing this over ssh?
Is it because systemctl suspend requires a password?
Is there an easier way or another tool to achieve the goal I am after?

This is probably a Windows-specific... quirk? vestige, even? -- but, it's interesting to me that the "Custom colors:" list can be populated from a datalist Element (via the list attribute), and also from within the dialog; but this state is lost when the dialog is closed, and it is re-initialized from the attached list with no state ever passed back to the document.
The MDN documentation for instance, doesn't mention anything specific, but I take that to mean there isn't anything currently developed for Firefox, nor stipulated in the underlying standard; but that doesn't mean no browsers support such means.
To be clear, I would expect -- if such a feature exists on any platform -- it might present as an array of color strings in the corresponding input event, or perhaps even the underling datalist is mutated to match (when so enabled by the document). But there are lots of ways this could be handled; my question is, was this ever done?
I'm also guessing, if such a feature exists anywhere at all, it's far from portable, so, I don't intend on using this for any actual content, just curious if this has been toyed with before.  And I expect there are more featureful libraries that provide such functionality natively [in JS and etc.], but this is also not my concern here.

The original problem: I want to allow cgi scripts to run, but only in the second directory, and I want to pass specific extensions to an interpreter.
I have set up a VirtualHost like the following:
<VirtualHost *:80>
  ServerName example.org

  Define document_root /data/example.org/site
  DocumentRoot ${document_root}

  RewriteCond "${script_dir}%{REQUEST_URI}" -f [OR]

Subject: =?us-ascii?Q?[Roger_Parkinson]_Please_moderate:_"Dummy_post?=

Dummy_post in this case is the name of my post and I can live with it not being in the subject line at all, or maybe just remove the quotes.
I have looked at several plugins that looked like they might do this but they turned out to be more interested in generating notifications for other events rather than customising the message for an existing event.
Is this possible? I'm okay editing PHP but I'd take a while to hunt out where it needs to change and the next update will overwrite the change unless I do something clever.

title: Parallelizing highly dynamic and unbalanced loads
text:
I have a computation with a following structure (pseudocode):
intermediate_results = []

for source in sources: # (1)
    source_data = prepare( load( source ) ) # (2)
    for sample in schedule_samples( source_data ): # (3)
        sample_data = extract_sample( source_data ) # (4)
        for result_data in postprocess_sample( sample_data ):
            intermediate_results.append( result_data )

final_results = []
for intermediate_result_group in group_intermediate_results( intermediate_results ):
    for final_result in compile_final_result( intermediate_result_group ):
        final_results.append( final_result )

The count of (1) is from 1-3 items to several thousands. The count of (3) is from hundreds to millions. And not known before actually loading data and processing it.
The (2) and (4) is very computation expensive procedures. The (2) is approximately ten times more costly than (4).
I need to parallelize the whole process in a relatively effective way.
My current implementation is based on python's multiprocessing module and parallelized only on loop (1). This is simple and working, but have an issue. Sometimes couple of sources have much more samples that others, so at the end of the process, several workers are processing such large sources, while others finished it tasks.
The relatively good solution for this process would be work sealing technique, when worker that finished it's job tries to get tasks from other workers.
Currently i need to scale this process to cluster with 10 nodes. So i thinking to use some kind of framework such as dask or ray to solve complex job scheduling.
But i've found that both of them are not very friendly to this kind of unbalanced nested dynamic workflows.
It is very simple to create dozens of independent jobs, each of that will independently load source data, but it will be very slow, so i need that tasks are able to reuse loaded data, without sacrificing ability to move work between them.
Is there any pythonic tools that could help to solve this kind of parallelization problem and how to use it correctly? Or it is better to create custom implementation?

title: Mount returns reason given by server: No such file or directory
text:
Yes! Another boring mount question :-) :
My home server had crashed - probably because 1 of the HDD has crashed - after removing it the server went back on without issues. note that there are 2 other drives in the server as well :
Disk2_1TB
Disk4_1TB
And the new disk :
Disk3_500GB (which replaces Disk3_250GB)
Now the fun starts.
The broken drive was a 250GB HDD drive - the new drive is a SDD drive.
Put it in - formatted it to NTFS, created a label changed details in the smb.conf - added an entry in /etc/fstab to mount it on boot and all is ok on server side.
**entry in Fstab (server):**
UUID=67EAAB18626D809E /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB auto defaults 0 0 

**Entry in smb.conf**
comment = Disk3_500GB
path = /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB
browseable = yes
read only = no
writeable = yes
valid users = me, you,
create mask = 0700
directory mask = 0700

**lsblk**
sdb                         8:16   0 931.5G  0 disk 
└─sdb1                      8:17   0 931.5G  0 part /mnt/rabbithole/Disk2_1TB
sdc                         8:32   0 931.5G  0 disk 
└─sdc1                      8:33   0 931.5G  0 part /mnt/rabbithole/Disk4_1TB
sdd                         8:48   0 465.8G  0 disk 
└─sdd1                      8:49   0 465.8G  0 part /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB

**sudo blkid -o list**
/dev/sdd1  ntfs    Disk3_500GB /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB 67EAAB18626D809E
/dev/sdb1  ntfs    sdb_1       /mnt/rabbithole/Disk2_1TB 3DF5D0052AA8C8AB
/dev/sdc1  ntfs    SDD_1       /mnt/rabbithole/Disk4_1TB 54D70D411ABCA6A2

you can see here that (swapping SATA cables inside the server) sdc1 USED to be SDD_1 - but i cannot imagine the label of the drive making all the difference.
ls -l 
drwxrwxrwx 1 root root 4096 Dec 24 13:09 Disk2_1TB
drwxrwxrwx 1 root root 4096 Dec 30 11:31 Disk3_500GB
drwxrwxrwx 1 root root 4096 Nov 21  2023 Disk4_1TB

now on the client side :
**/etc/fstab**
192.168.178.100:/mnt/rabbithole/Disk2_1TB /mnt/rabbithole/Disk2_1TB nfs4 defaults,x-systemd.after=wait-for-ping.service 0 0
192.168.178.100:/mnt/rabbithole/Disk4_1TB /mnt/rabbithole/Disk4_1TB nfs4 defaults,x-systemd.after=wait-for-ping.service 0 0
192.168.178.100:/mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB nfs4 defaults,x-systemd.after=wait-for-ping.service 0 0


**output sudo mount -a**
mount.nfs4: mounting 192.168.178.100:/mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB failed, reason given by server: No such file or directory

Now when i use Dolphin and go to 'Shared Folders (SMB)' and go to smb//192.168.178.100 it finds the drive perfectly and i am able to browse the files within.
Now being the smartass i then tried using the cli to see if i could play a bit with the mount command - but without success.
  326  sudo mount -t nfs4 //192.168.178.100/mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB/
  327  sudo mount -t nfs4 //192.168.178.100/mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB/ /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB/
  328  sudo mount -t nfs //192.168.178.100/mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB/

  331  sudo mount 192.168.178.100:mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB /mnt/rabbithole/Disk3_500GB/

all without succes - i did get a -2 error somewhere - but not sure when i got that one.
then i had the idea to mount 1 level higher :
192.168.178.100:/mnt/rabbithole/ /mnt/rabbithole/ nfs4 defaults,x-systemd.after=wait-for-ping.service 0 0

Which gives me Disk2 and Disk4 drives in dolphin (but not the 500GB drive)
so - i think i did everything right - but for some (probably stupid) reason the disk cannot be mounted as it was not there.
Hope that anybody can help me out here.
Regards

Load smb config files from /etc/samba/smb.conf

which (I guess) is a consequence of the condition which produces the warning message issued by testparm.

title: Why File Size Increases When Converting MP4 to WebM
text:
I'm trying to convert a MP4 file to WebM, using the following parameters:
./ffmpeg -y -hide_banner -nostats \
-i /usr/local/m2/static/lotteon-low-bitrate.mp4 \
-threads auto -f webm -acodec libopus -b:a 96.059k -vcodec libsvtav1 -preset 11 -pix_fmt yuv420p \
-vf "scale='min(-1, iw)':'min(-1,ih)':force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,crop=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2" \
"/usr/local/m2/m2temp/xcdrtmp/test.webm"

However, the output webm file size is larger than the source MP4 file. For example:

Source MP4: 4.6 MB (bit rate: 994,053 bps)
Output WebM: 16 MB (bit rate: 3,902,037 bps)

I know SVT-AV1 encoder defaults to CRF mode. Due to not specifying the bitrate explicitly, the SVT-AV1 encoder automatically sets the bit_rate. It appears that the encoder is setting it to a much higher value (3,323,104 bps), causing the increase in file size compared to the source MP4 (994,053 bps). Here are the methods i tried to reduce the WebM file size compared to the source MP4:
-b:v 994k

I tried to match the target bitrate with the source MP4's bitrate to reduce the output size, but encountered the following error:
Svt[error]: Instance 1: Force key frames is not supported for VBR mode Last message r
epeated 2 times [libsvtav1 @ 0x239dd100] Error setting encoder parameters: bad parameter (0x80001005)
Looking at the official documentation, this mode change (from CRF to VBR when setting a target bitrate) appears to be expected behavior. However, the error is puzzling since I haven't set any force keyframe parameters in the FFmpeg command.


svtav1-params "mbr=994k"

The second method i tried was using the svtav1-params "mbr=994k" option to set the maxrate while maintaining CRF mode. This method showed some improvement, but the output file size was still larger than the source MP4.

Output WebM: 5MB (bit rate: 1,209,877 bps)

The more critical reason why we can't adopt the second method (using svtav1-params "mbr=994k") is that even for the same MP4 source file, the output file size varies slightly with each encoding.
-b:v 994k -svtav1-params “rc=2:pred-struct=1”(CBR, low delay)

The final method I tried was setting the target bitrate while using CBR (Constant Bit Rate) and low-delay mode. The default value for pred-structure is 2(random access), but I had to use low-delay mode due to the following error:
Svt[error]: CBR Rate control is currently not supported for SVT_AV1_PRED_RANDOM_ACCESS, use VBR mode
This way was the only approach among those i tried that successfully reduced the output size.


Output WebM: 4.3MB (bit rate: 1,032,373 bps)

In summary, I have three questions about this MP4 to WebM conversion issue:

When setting the target bitrate with -b:v 994k, the switch to VBR
mode is expected behavior. However, why does the force keyframe
error occur when we haven't explicitly set any force keyframe
parameters?
Why does the output WebM file size fluctuate when setting maxrate
either through -maxrate or svtav1-params "mbr=994k", even when using
the same MP4 source file?
Besides using -b:v 994k -svtav1-params "rc=2:pred-struct=1" (CBR
with low delay), are there any other methods that can guarantee a
WebM output size smaller than the source MP4 when converting from
MP4 to WebM?

I am using a recent version of the SVT-AV1 codec:
Svt[info]: SVT [version]:       SVT-AV1 Encoder Lib 58146ca
Svt[info]: SVT [build]  :       GCC 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-2)   64 bit
Svt[info]: LIB Build date: Oct 28 2024 07:40:59
ffmpeg video svt-av1

Initially, there were a lot of "Static surface pool size exceeded".
decode_receive_frame_internal failed = Invalid data found when processing input
Static surface pool size exceeded
get_buffer() failed
thread_get_buffer() failed
decode_slice_headec error
no frame!

This got fixed by incrementing initial_pool_size by 3. Now the following two flows works as expected:

./ffmpeg.exe -hwaccel d3d11va -hwaccel_output_format d3d11 -hide_banner -i bbb_sunflower_2160p_30fps_normal.mp4 -hw_encoding 1 -c:v h264_mf -vframes 100 -loglevel verbose sample.mp4 -y
./ffmpeg.exe -hwaccel d3d11va -hwaccel_output_format d3d11 -hide_banner -i bbb_sunflower_2160p_30fps_normal.mp4 -hw_encoding 1 -c:v h264_mf -vf "scale_d3d11=width=1920:height=1080" -vframes 100 -loglevel verbose sample.mp4 -y

When I try to call av_hwframe_transfer_data() within the if(encoder_requires_software_frame) block for the following flow, "Static surface pool size exceeded" occurs once again.

./ffmpeg.exe -hwaccel d3d11va -hwaccel_output_format d3d11 -hide_banner -i bbb_sunflower_2160p_30fps_normal.mp4 -c:v rawvideo -vframes 10 -loglevel verbose sample.yuv -y

title: What are the downsides of PARTIAL backups?
text:
I have recently found online this amazing article about partial backups by Alexandr Omelchenko

-- this is how he would do a backup:

BACKUP DATABASE your_database TO DISK = 'full.bak'
BACKUP DATABASE your_database READ_WRITE_FILEGROUPS TO DISK = 'partial_backup_full.bak'
BACKUP DATABASE your_database READ_WRITE_FILEGROUPS TO DISK = 'partial_backup_diff.bak' WITH DIFFERENTIAL

-- this is how he would do a restore:

RESTORE DATABASE your_database FROM DISK = 'full.bak' WITH NORECOVERY 
GO 
RESTORE DATABASE your_dataabse FROM DISK = 'partial_backup_full.bak' WITH NORECOVERY  
GO 
RESTORE DATABASE your_database FROM DISK = 'partial_backup_diff.bak' WITH RECOVERY  
GO

It happens that I have a few databases that have 4 filegroups. One of these file groups is loaded with documents that are saved inside a table in that filegroup.
I think I could benefit from backing up the filegroups separately.
What would be the possible drawbacks in doing that? Other than the overhead of altering the restore verifyonly, including dbaTools, to accommodate this change and making sure taking backups with checksums?
Something I would need to check is compression.
Another thing is checksum option on for the backups - as suggested by the man himself - Ola - here and Paul Randal here.
We definitely need to check if our backups are reliable.

title: Claim related to symmetry of stationarity
text:
On p. 113 of Cryer's Time Series Analysis, in the context of ACFs and partial ACFs, I read

Consider predicting $ Y_t $ based on a linear function of the
intervening variables $ Y_{t-1}, Y_{t-2}, \ldots, Y_{t-k+1} $, say,
$$ \beta_1 Y_{t-1} + \beta_2 Y_{t-2} + \cdots + \beta_{k-1} Y_{t-k+1},$$
with the $ \beta $'s chosen to minimize the mean square error of
prediction. If we assume that the $ \beta $'s have been so chosen and
then think backward in time, it follows from stationarity that the
best “predictor” of $ Y_{t-k} $ based on the same $ Y_{t-1}, Y_{t-2},\ldots, Y_{t-k+1} $ will be
$$ \beta_1 Y_{t-k+1} + \beta_2 Y_{t-k+2} + \cdots + \beta_{k-1}Y_{t-1}. $$

This statement "reverses" the coefficients, in a way suggests that stationarity is symmetric. This seems counter-intuitive to me; could anyone help verify this result?
For example, one simple case of this claim is that if $c$ is the optimal coefficient for $Y_{t} = cY_{t-1}$, then $Y_{t-1} = cY_{t}$.

I was wondering if anyone has any thoughts on this? Am I seeing an overfitting case? Or does this "performance fluctuations" simply due to the nature of the problem? (i.e. if I only have ~10 cases per month, of course just by detecting 1 extra case, I can 'raise' my recall by 10%).

title: Issues with Low $I^2$ in Multivariate Random-Effects Meta-Analysis of DLNMs
text:
Summary: Hi, using R, I am conducting a multivariate random-effects meta-analysis of DLNMs (distributed lag non-linear model) with a quasi-Poisson link that includes 400 studies (two-stage time series design). The results show a very low $I^2$ value, narrow confidence intervals and correlations of $1.0$ (or close to $1.0$) among the random-effects (co)variance components.
Context & Goal: The goal is to better understand the effect of region-specific environmental predictors (operationalized as its region-specific percentile) on a health count outcome. While there is substantive variability across regions in stage 1 results, the low $I^2$ suggests near homogeneity. I'm uncertain if these results are due to model specification, data properties, or another issue.
Key observations in the meta analysis:

$I^2$ is low at around $1\%$, contrary to expectations given the
variability across regions of Stage 1 results.
Narrow confidence intervals, especially along the lagged space of the
predictor.
Correlations of $1.0$ in the random-effects (co)variance components.
The observed effects of the main predictor on the outcome seem, however, valid and match expectations.

Specific Questions:

What might be causing the low $I^2$ values and narrow confidence
intervals in my meta-analysis, and how can I investigate possible
issues?
Are the perfect correlations in my variance components an issue? If
so, are there adjustments available or further tests necessary?
Is the vast variability in population size something to worry about?

Some additional info:

I reduced stage 1 estimates to make the meta-analysis more efficient, but the problem also occurs with non-reduced analyses.
The issue persists if a fixed-effects meta-analysis is used instead
of a random-effects one. In general, there is little difference in
the estimates of the fixed effects between models.
I used the dlnm package for stage 1 analyses and the mixmeta package for stage 2 analysis.
I repeated analyses, omitting one county every time, but the $I^2$ would only fluctuate around $0.5$ to $1.5$% (roughly), so I concluded it was no one county that was an influential case.

Any suggestion would be really appreciated :)
Simplyfied R-Code:
    library(dlnm)
    library(mixmeta)
    
    nd_lag <- nd_lag_use
    nk_lag <- nk_lag_use
    klag <- logknots(nd_lag,nk=nk_lag)  
    ktemp <- c(.10, .75, .90)
    dfperyear <- 8
    linkfamily <- quasipoisson()
    
    coefs <- matrix(NA, nrow=length(list_regions), ncol=(length(ktemp)+1)*(nk_lag+2))
    vcovs <- as.list(rep(NA, length(list_regions)))
    names(vcovs) <- rownames(coefs) <- list_regions
    
    coefs_reduced <- matrix(NA, nrow=length(list_regions), ncol=length(ktemp)+1)
    vcovs_reduced <- as.list(rep(NA, length(list_regions)))
    names(vcovs_reduced) <- rownames(coefs_reduced) <- list_regions
   
    
    for(regionID in list_regions){
      
      data_interm <- list_data[[regionID]]  %>% arrange(time)
      
      basis <- crossbasis(data_interm$predictor,
                          argvar=list(knots=ktemp, fun="ns"),
                          arglag=list(knots=klag, fun="ns", intercept=TRUE),
                          lag=nd_lag)
      
      model <- glm(outcome ~  basis  + ns(time, dfperyear*10) + dayofweek + school_holiday,
                   family=linkfamily,
                   data_interm)
      
      model.class <- class(model)
      model.link <- dlnm:::getlink(model,model.class)
      
      crosspredictions <- crosspred(basis,model,cen=.5)
      coefs[regionID, ] <- coef(crosspredictions)
      vcovs[[regionID]] <- vcov(crosspredictions)
      

      reduced_estimates <- crossreduce(basis, model, cen=.50)

      coefs_reduced[regionID, ] <- coef(reduced_estimates)
      vcovs_reduced[[regionID]] <- vcov(reduced_estimates)
    
    }
    
    meta_overall <- mixmeta(coefs_reduced, vcovs_reduced, data=data_county_names, random=~1|regionID)
    meta_overall_popsize <- mixmeta(coefs_reduced~0+population_size, vcovs_reduced, data=data_regions, random=~1|regionID)

    summary(meta_overall)
    summary(meta_overall_popsize)

title: How to define and train a function $f(x,y)$ with a boundary condition?
text:
I have a dataset consisting of triplets $(x_i,y_i,z_i), i=1,2,\cdots,N$, where $x_i,y_i,z_i\in \mathbb{R}$. My goal is to find a function $f(x,y)$ that satisfies the following conditions:

Boundary condition: $f(x, 0)=x, \forall x\in\mathbb{R}$
Target approximation: $f(x_i, y_i)\approx z_i, i=1,2,\cdots,N$

This can be expressed as a constrained optimization problem:
$$\min_f\sum_{i=1}^{N}\ell(f(x_i,y_i),z_i)\\\text{s.t. }f(x,0)=x$$
where $\ell(\cdot,\cdot)$ is a loss function.
My Approach: Let $f(x,y)=x+yg(x,y)$, and then train function $g$.
Questions:

Is this approach to enforce the boundary condition appropriate and robust?
Are there alternative ways to model $f(x,y)$ that might simplify or improve this formulation?
From a statistical perspective, how should I interpret this problem? For example, would modeling $p(z|x,y)$ explicitly as a probabilistic model (e.g., Gaussian) provide additional benefits?

Thank you for your insights and suggestions!

title: Two equal symmetric bilinear forms.
text:
Note that the second fundamental form is completely determined by its values of the form $\text{II}(v,v)$ for unit vectors $v$, by the following lemma.
Lemma 8.11 Suppose $V$ is an inner product space, $W$ is a vector space, and $B,B':V \times V \to W$ are symmetric and bilinear. If $B(v,v) = B'(v,v)$ for every unit vector $v \in V$, then $B = B'$.
Proof. Every vector $v \in V$ can be written $v = \lambda \hat v$ [SIC] for some unit vector $\hat v$, so the bilinearity of $B$ and $B'$ implies $B(v,v) = B'(v,v)$ for every $v$, not just unit vectors. The result then follows from the following polarization identity, which is proved in exactly the same way as its counterpart for inner products:
$$
B(v,w) = \tfrac 14 (B(v+w,v+w) - B(v-w,v-w)). \qquad \qquad \square
$$

(image from textbook)
Problem: Suppose $V$ is an inner product space, $W$ vector space and $B,B'$ are symmetric and blinear. If $B(v,v) = B'(v,v)$ for every unit vector then the two bilinear forms are equal $B = B'.$

title: Is this proof for problem 3.19 in Baby Rudin correct?
text:
Problem 3.19 in Baby Rudin, states

Associate to each sequence $a=\{a_n\}$, in which $a_n$ is $0$ or $2$, the real number $$x(a) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{a_n}{3^n}$$ Prove that the set of all $x(a)$ is precisely the Cantor set.

I wrote a proof for this problem, but I am not sure if it is correct and there is a part (in bold) which I am not sure is justified.
My proof: 
Lemma 1  The left and right endpoints of the cantor set can be expressed by $$\left[\sum_{n=1}^N \frac{a_n}{3^n} + \sum_{n=N+1}^\infty \frac{0}{3^n}\right] \text{ and } \left[\sum_{n=1}^N \frac{a_n}{3^n} + \sum_{n=N+1}^\infty \frac{2}{3^n}\right]$$ respectively for some $N\in\mathbb{N}$. 
Left Endpoints:
WTS that by dividing each $C_n$ in half, when left endpoint $x$ is on left side, $a_1 = 0$ when it is on right side, $a_1=2$, then by taking the half that $x$ is on and dividing again, $a_1,a_2,...,a_n$ can be found through this process. The rest, $a_{n+1}, ... =0$. So, for example, for $C_4$ and the left endpoint $a=\frac{2}{27}$. "a" is on the left side of $C_4$, so $a_1=0$, of that side, it is again on the left so $a_2=0$, than it is on the right $a_3=2$, than it is on the left half of that section, $a_4=0$. $0+0+\frac{2}{3^3}+0 = \frac{2}{27}$.
Base case: $C_1 = [0,\frac{1}{3}] \cup [\frac{2}{3},1]$. Clearly, $0= \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{0}{3^n}$ and $ \frac{2}{3} = \frac{2}{3} + \sum_{n=2}^\infty 0$ 
Inductive step: Assume that each left endpoint $x$ in $C_n$ has this property where a sequence of $\{a_n\}$ can be found by the dividing process. Consider $C_{n+1}$. If $x$ is carried over from $C_n$ than the formula is the same, with $a_{n+1} = 0$ since $x$ is on the left half of the original interval in $C_n$. If $x$ is "new'', than $a_{n+1} = 2$ since it is on the right side of the split interval, so $\frac{2}{3^{n+1}}$ is added compared to the process to get to the the left side of the split interval which is carred over from $C_n$. 
Right Endpoints:
Similarly, for right endpoints in $C_n$ the exact same process of assigning values to $a_n$ is done except now for $k>n$, $a_n=2$.
Theorem 1  Problem 3.19 
$\implies$ If $x$ is an endpoint of $\mathcal{C}$, than it can be expressed as $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{a_n}{3^n}$ by the lemma above. If $x$ is not an endpoint than it is a limit point of a sequence of endpoints (since $\mathcal{C}$ is perfect), $\{s_n\}$ where $s_k$ is the left endpoint in the interval containing $x$ in $C_k$. So $\{s_n\} = \{\frac{a_1}{3}, \frac{a_1}{3} + \frac{a_2}{3^2}, ...\}$. This sequence of partial sums converges to $x$ so that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{a_n}{3^n} = x$.

But since each term in the sequence is a left endpoint of $\mathcal{C}$ that means there exists a sequence in $\mathcal{C}$ which converges to $x$, but since $\mathcal{C}$ is compact, $x\in\mathcal{C}$

title: No holomorphic functions on $T\mathbb{P}^1$
text:
Is it true that $H^0(T\mathbb{P}^1,\mathcal{O}_{T\mathbb{P^1}})=\mathbb{C}$? I think it should be, any function $f$ has to be constant on the zero section and also on the projective curves gotten by deforming the zero section along the normal bundle to it, we can do that because there is a non zero global holomorphic vector field on $\mathbb{P}^1$, and these cover all of $T\mathbb{P}^1$, and have non empty intersections with one another because of the hairy ball theorem, so $f$ is a constant. The same argument should work if we replace $T\mathbb{P}^1$ with $T^\vee\Sigma$ with $g_\Sigma \geq 2$. Is there a cleaner argument? This one sounds shady. I tried to make it say something absurd for $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{A}^1$ but it doesn't, because the only projective curves on that surface are the translates $\mathbb{P}^1\times\{\lambda\}$ I think.
By contrast if we replace tangent bundle by cotangent bundle, then we have a lot of functions, because the cotangent bundle to $\mathbb{P}^1$ has a birational morphism to an affine quadric surface. But in this case the zero section is rigid so there is no contradiction.

title: Irreducible topological space definition
text:
A topological space X is called reducible if $X=X_1 \cup X_2$ for closed subsets $X_1, X_2\subsetneq X$. And $X$ is irreducible if $X \neq \emptyset$ and X is not reducible.

This is the definition I found for reducible and irreducible topological spaces when I was reading Commutative Algebra. Also $\mathbb{C}$ with Zariski topology is irreducible (In fact every $n$ dimensional affine space over an algebraically closed field $k$ is irreducible with Zariski topology) since $I(\mathbb{C}^n)=(0)$ and it is a prime ideal in $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Also I reckon that $\mathbb{C}$ is a Noetherian topological space. But all of these doesn't add up when it comes to the following theorem

Every Noetherian topological space $X\neq \emptyset$ is a finite union of irreducible closed subsets of $X$ $\implies X=X_1 \cup \dots X_r$ where $X_i$'s are closed subsets of $X$.

Doesn't that make $X$ reducible as per definition? Actually isn't it making every Noetherian topological space reducible? Then $\mathbb{C}$ should be reducible as well which is not true when equipped with Zariski topology. What am I missing/done wrong here?
Edit: Also the proof of this theorem is by method of contradiction and the assumption that $X$ is not a finite union of irreducible closed subsets leads to the conclusion $X$ is reducible. But what if $X$ is a union of infinite irreducible closed sets. How can one say that $X$ is reducible from that ?

title: Existence of nonzero global section of dual of a locally free sheaf with a surjection
text:
Let $X$ be a projective variety, and let $D$ is an effective divisor on $X$.
Suppose the map $\mathcal{E} \rightarrow \mathcal{O}_D$ is a surjective map between sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Assumne further that $\mathcal{E}$ is locally free.
As we can consider a tensor product $\;\cdot\;\otimes\mathcal{O}_D$ is an right exact functor, we also get a surjection
$$
f:\mathcal{E}_{|D} \rightarrow \mathcal{O}_{D}
$$
between the sheaves as an $\mathcal{O}_{D}$-modules. Once I read from a literature, there is a statement that
$\textit{Since $\mathcal{E}$ is locally free, $\mathcal{E}_{|D}$ is also locally free. Hence $f$ induces a non-zero element of $\;\mathrm{H}^0(\mathcal{E}^{\vee}_{|D})$}$.
This may be true, but why the argument about the locall freeness of $\mathcal{E}$ is needed?
I think if a sequence of $\mathcal{O}_{D}$-modules $$\mathcal{E}_{|D}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{D}\rightarrow 0$$
is exact, takinig a functor $\mathcal{Hom}(-,\mathcal{O}_D)$ we have an exact sequence
$$
0 \rightarrow \mathcal{O}_{D} \rightarrow \mathcal{E}^{\vee}_{|D} \rightarrow\cdots.
$$
Thus, we just have $\;\mathrm{H}^0(\mathcal{E}^{\vee}_{|D})\neq 0$ without the locally freeness assumption for $\mathcal{E}$.

title: On the classification of finite schemes over the reals
text:
As part of Humanity's Last Exam I wanted to enter a question about (counting) the equivalence classes of finite schemes over the reals of length 4 resp. 5. Two referees suggested that this can be found on Math Stack Exchange resp. algebraic geometry textbooks. However, I searched and could not find the sources hinted at.
Denote the base field by $k$. Note, that the scheme classification can also be phrased in terms of classifying (commutative) finite length $k$-algebras $A$. The length will be denoted by $n=\text{rk}_k(A)$.
For algebraically closed fields Bjorn Poonen showed in 2006 that (independent of $\text{char}(k)$) there are finitely many equivalence classes if and only if $n\leq 6$. In that paper he also gave the classification for $n\leq 6$ - the actual classification being dependent on the characteristic. Onda also gave a classification in the case $n=7$ and $\text{char}(k)\in\{2,3\}$, which was the last missing part for a complete classification in case $n=7$. But the field $k=\mathbb{R}$ is not algebraically closed, although Poonen discusses in Remark 2.2 a construction of infinitely many equivalence classes for $n>6$, $|k|=\infty$ and $\text{char}(k)\neq 2$ which obviously includes $k=\mathbb{R}$.
There is a paper in Spanish that might be relevant, but unfortunately I do not speak Spanish.

title: Expected Cost of Book Selection with Varying Selection Probabilities and Position-Dependent Costs
text:
I am working on a problem involving the expected cost of selecting books from a stack in two different ways, and I would appreciate some insights, particularly regarding the case when $m \to \infty$.
There are $n$ books in a stack, numbered from 1 to $n$, initially arranged in increasing order from top to bottom. Each book $k$ has a selection probability $p_k$, which depends on the book itself, i.e., $p_k$ is the probability of selecting the $k$-th book (not necessarily corresponding to its position in the stack). The cost of selecting the $k$-th book, when counting from the top, is $a_k$, and this cost depends on the book's position in the stack (i.e., the cost increases as the position in the stack goes down).
Two methods are used for selecting the books:

Method 1: A book is selected randomly, and then it is placed back in the same position.
Method 2: A book is selected randomly, and after selection, it is placed at the top of the stack.

I am interested in calculating the expected cost of selecting $m$ books, under both methods. For Method 1, the expected cost is straightforward, and it is given by $mN$, where
$$\displaystyle N = \sum_{k=1}^{n} p_k a_k $$
This result holds because each selection is independent, and the cost per selection is the same across all selections.
However, for Method 2, the situation is more complex. After each selection, the book is placed at the top of the stack, which changes the positions of the other books, altering their associated costs in subsequent selections. I believe this introduces a random process that is more difficult to analyze, and I’m not sure how to compute the expected cost in this case. I think Markov chain will be involved.
Additionally, I would like to know what happens as $m \to \infty$. My hypothesis is that, when $p_k$ is decreasing, the expected cost for both methods should converge to the same value in the limit. I am uncertain if this is correct, so I would appreciate any insights or formal arguments to confirm or refute this.
Finally, if $a_k$ is difficult to estimate, I could approximate it as an arithmetic sequence: $a_k = a_0 + kd$. How would this assumption affect the analysis, and how could I estimate the expected cost more easily under this approximation?

title: Existence of analytic metrics on analytic manifolds
text:
Let $X$ be a real analytic manifold, and let $E$ be a real analytic vector bundle. Does there always exist an analytic metric on $E$? By analytic metric I mean that if $U \subset X$ is an analytic chart, with analytic trivialisation $E|_U \cong \mathbb R^r \times U$, the coefficients of the metric are analytic.
Usually, the existence of metrics on vector bundles is proved by choosing local trivializations $E|_{U_i} \cong \mathbb R^r \times U_i$, and then gluing the standard metrics using a partition of unity, subordinate to $\{U_i\}$. However, partitions of unity are famously non-analytic, so the resulting metric is also not analytic.
Any reference would be appreciated.

Context: Existence of analytic metrics appears in Voisin's Hodge theory and complex algebraic geometry, I, proof of Proposition 9.5. In that case, $\mathcal X$ is a complex manifold, $X_0 \subset \mathcal X$ is a compact complex submanifold, and one needs an analytic metric on $\mathcal X$ in a neighbourhood of $X_0$. The aim is to produce a tubular neighbourhood whose fibers are analytic submanifolds of $\mathcal X$.
